 REVA University hosts first literature festival 'The First Chapter'; honours students for academic excellence
 REVA University hosts first literature festival 'The First Chapter'; honours students for academic excellence
 Soumi Roy | October 31, 2026 | 02:21 PM IST | 1 min read 
 The first edition of the two-day festival features author interactions, panel discussions, poetry sessions, book talks and Kannada theatre performances.
 REVA University inaugurates its first literature festival. (Image: Press Release) 
 REVA University has inaugurated the first edition of its literature festival, ‘The First Chapter’, on its campus on October 30, 2026. Held under the theme ‘Two Days, Countless Stories’, the two-day festival saw authors, writers, journalists, artists and students celebrating books, literature and storytelling.
 Welcoming the guests and speaking about the importance of
 literature festivals
 , Dr Shyama Raju, Chancellor, REVA University, said, “REVA Literature Festival provides a platform for students and literary enthusiasts to engage with diverse voices, appreciate the richness of literature and discover the joy of reading."
 Speaking at the event, Suchendra Prasad, an actor who has highlighted the importance of reading, said that books can have a strong influence on the minds of young people. Referring to the legacy of Ravi Belagere, he encouraged students to develop an interest in reading and treat it as an enriching experience.

 REVA Literature Festival features theatre, book talks
 The festival, held on October 30 and 31, showcases panel discussions, author interactions, book talks, masterclasses, poetry sessions, open mic performances and a book fair. As part of the Ninasam Tour 2026, Kannada plays will also be staged on the campus.
 Emphasising REVA’s vision, Dr Shyama Raju said, “At REVA, we believe in not just giving degrees but imparting multidisciplinary education and encouraging students to
 learn beyond the classroom
 . The first chapter of REVA Literature Festival is a reflection of this belief. Such platforms provide opportunities for students to explore ideas, engage with different perspectives and discover the world through literature and the arts.”
 The university also presented the ‘Prathibha Puraskara’ to students from government schools in Doddaballapura and Jakkur, and REVA PU Colleges in Kattigenahalli, Ganga Nagar and Sanjay Nagar for their academic achievements.
